[USER] User thinks they might have an anxious attachment style.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To identify attachment styles, individuals can take an attachment style quiz, reflect on past relationships, or seek insight from a therapist.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Anxious attachment style may lead to being overly clingy and paranoid about a partner leaving, while avoidant attachment style may result in emotional distance and pushing partners away.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended resources for learning more about attachment styles include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. "Attached: The New Science of Adult Attachment and How It Can Help You Find - and Keep - Love" by Amir Levine and Rachel Heller.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. "Hold Me Tight: Seven Conversations for a Lifetime of Love" by Dr. Sue Johnson.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. The PsychAlive website, which offers articles and resources on adult attachment styles and relationship issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. The Gottman Institute, which provides research-based methods for improving relationships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Counseling or therapy with a trained therapist experienced in attachment issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested specific actions for improving relationships with an anxious attachment style include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Be aware of tendencies like feeling anxious or clingy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Communicate with your partner about anxious feelings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Develop self-love and self-compassion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Practice mindfulness through meditation or deep breathing exercises.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Seek professional help if needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Remember that attachment styles can change over time with self-reflection and personal growth.
